mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in periods of falling GDP.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over two months indicates a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during these episodes compared to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average and UNRATE stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during these episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average signals a recovery in residential construction, which boosts demand for building materials and related equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of sustained HOUST recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) and Industrial Production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months signals broad-based demand weakness, which reduces earnings across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and INDPRO both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during these episodes.
